Henry III appears as the addressee and principal recipient of the papal mandate regarding the Sicilian business.

persons: Henry III, King of England (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Henry III, King of England, urging him to receive Master Gervase of London (subdeacon and canon of Lichfield) and his associates back into royal favour, now that a dispute between the Bishop of Hereford and Master Gervase over various articles has been amicably settled. persons: Louis IX, Roi de France (beneficiary)

persons: Willem II Graaf van Hollant en Zeeland (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Willem II, King of the Romans and Count of Holland, informing him that rebellious men from Frisia, submitting to his lordship, have granted him and his heirs the tithes of all their possessions in the county of Holland in perpetuity. This is a one-sided grant/permission with no active dispute as the operative matter; Willem II is the addressee/beneficiary.

persons: Louis IX, Roi de France (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV renews for King Louis IX of France a privilege originally granted by Gregory IX, prohibiting anyone from placing the king's chapels under ecclesiastical interdict without special licence from the Apostolic See. This is a one-sided renewal of a privilege in favour of the French crown; no dispute is involved. Louis IX is the addressee and beneficiary of the privilege.

This is a straightforward apostolic confirmation of an ecclesiastical property grant; there is no dispute. Frederick II appears only as the former owner of the palace.

persons: Henry III, King of England (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the Archbishop of York and his suffragans to collect in their cities and dioceses the tenth of ecclesiastical revenues, redemptions of crusade vows, legacies, and fruits of vacant benefices granted for five years to King Henry III of England for the prosecution of his crusade vow. Henry III is the matched beneficiary of the grant. This is a one-sided administrative/fiscal mandate in support of crusade financing, with no live dispute.

persons: Henry III, King of England (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to all archbishops and bishops in England, informing them that although he has obligated their churches and goods to certain merchants up to certain sums by reason of a tithe granted to King Henry III of England for the Sicilian business, it is his intention that these obligations shall not be proceeded upon unless a settlement of the Sicilian affair between the Roman Church and the king is reached. This is a unilateral papal communication/reassurance to the English episcopate, not an active dispute. Henry III appears only as the incidental beneficiary of the tithe grant mentioned in the background.

persons: Manfredo I von Hohenstaufen, King of Naples and Sicily (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV commands the commune of Fermo (Commune Firmanum) under penalty of 1000 pounds not to receive any envoys of Manfred of Hohenstaufen, who is described as "he who is called prince" and identified as an adversary of the Church. This is an operative papal mandate in the context of the political-military conflict between the papacy and Manfred over southern Italy. Manfred von Hohenstaufen appears as the named adversary/subject of the prohibition; the commune of Fermo is the addressee and principal obligated party.

persons: Henry III, King of England (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to the councillors and magnates of the kingdom of England, reporting that he has received their envoys (the archbishops of Embrun and Caratase, and Master Rustand the chaplain) and responded to their petitions. He also explains his delay in sending a legate, and expresses distress over accusations the envoys raised against the bishop-elect of Winchester. This is a diplomatic/administrative letter, not a live dispute before the papal court. King Henry III of England appears only as the monarch whose councillors are addressed and whose envoys are mentioned.

persons: Henry III, King of England (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV informs Henry III, King of England, that the Archbishop of Tarantaise and the Bishops of Bath and Wells have assigned 4,500 marks sterling from the ecclesiastical tithe revenues of England to Sienese merchants (Pietro Scotti Dominici, Giacomo Baglioni, etc.) for the improvement and reform of conditions in the apostolic privilege concerning the grant of the Kingdom of Sicily and for the discharge of a debt owed by the king and his sons. The pope urges Henry III to repay these merchants promptly. This is a one-sided papal communication regarding financial arrangements tied to the Sicilian business, with Henry III as the addressee/principal.

persons: Johann I Markgraf von Brandenburg (subject_or_mention) | Otto III Markgraf von Brandenburg (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the deans of Merseburg and Erfurt churches and the provost of Ratzeburg to compel Johann I and Otto III, Margraves of Brandenburg, to restore the county of Seehausen and three castles to Archbishop Rudolf and the church of Magdeburg. The castles and county had been granted to the margraves as a fief by Ludolph, bishop of Halberstadt. The dispute is between the Margraves of Brandenburg (lay) and the Archbishop/church of Magdeburg (ecclesiastical) over ecclesiastical property. Both matched Peerage persons (Johann I and Otto III) are principal parties as the defendants ordered to make restitution.

persons: Pietro II Conte di Savoia (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV confirms an exchange (permutatio) between Pietro II of Savoy and the abbot and convent of Saint-Maurice d'Agaune, whereby the abbey granted Pietro their house at Commugny (de Comuniaco) with its goods in the parish of Saint-Loup and at Versoix. This is a straightforward papal confirmation of a property exchange with no opposing party. Pietro II of Savoy is the matched beneficiary of the exchange.

persons: Edmund 'Crouchback' Plantagenet, Earl of Leicester (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV instructs his subdeacon and notary Master Arloto to extend the deadline (to the next three months from the upcoming Kalends of June) previously granted for reforming the business of the Kingdom of Sicily, and to extend the suspension of penalties and reservation of rights acquired over that kingdom. The document concerns the papal management of the Sicilian affair on behalf of Edmund Plantagenet, who appears as the beneficiary ("Edmundo regi Siciliae"). There is no live dispute between opposing parties; this is a procedural/administrative extension of terms.

persons: Jaime I, Rey de AragÃ³n (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to King James I of Aragon (the matched addressee) urging him to support the bishop of Segorbe (Segobricensis episcopus) and ensure that everything of which the bishop claims to have been despoiled is restored to him. The dispute is between the bishop of Segorbe on one side and the bishop and archdeacon of Valencia on the other — all ecclesiastical parties. King James I of Aragon appears as the addressee being asked to intervene in favor of the Segorbe bishop, not as a principal disputant himself.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (requestor)
summary: Pope Alexander IV, responding to a complaint by Thibaut, Count of Champagne (matched), mandates the Bishop of Langres (Gui) that bigamous clerks and married clerks who engage in commerce (wine, cloth, wool) or practice usury are not entitled to clerical privilege and must bear ordinary lay burdens. This is an administrative/disciplinary ruling, not a live dispute between parties. Thibaut appears as the requestor/complainant prompting the papal instruction directed at the Bishop of Langres.

persons: Louis IX, Roi de France (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants an indult to Louis IX, King of France, permitting him to distribute to the poor goods that have come to him by various means but cannot be restored to their rightful owners (because those persons cannot be found), and to receive full absolution for such distributions. This is a one-sided papal grant/privilege with no opposing party. Louis IX is the sole beneficiary and matched principal.
domain_other_detail: papal indult / almsgiving dispensation with plenary absolution

persons: Henry III, King of England (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to John Mansel, Treasurer of York, urging him to persuade Henry III, King of England, to be favorable to Sienese merchants, to whom 4,500 marks sterling from the English tithe had been assigned, so that they might obtain what they are owed. This is a one-sided papal exhortation/request with no live dispute being adjudicated. Henry III appears only as the target of the requested persuasion, not as a party to litigation.
domain_other_detail: papal intercession regarding debt/financial obligation to merchants

persons: BÃ©la IV ArpÃ¡d, King of Hungary (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to King Béla IV of Hungary urging him to pay the Knights Hospitaller (Order of St John of Jerusalem) 1,000 marks of silver annually, a sum his father had promised them from the royal treasury, which Béla had been delaying beyond due time. The pope also instructs him to honour the privileges, immunities, and liberties agreed with the Order and to make good on arrears. This is a one-sided papal exhortation/mandate, not a live dispute before the Church. Béla IV is the addressee and principal subject of the letter.

persons: Ulrich III Herzog von KÃ¤rnten (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the Prior of S. Giorgio in Allega to publicly declare Ulrich III, Duke of Carinthia, excommunicated and his lands under interdict. The Bishop of Castellano had already promulgated a sentence of excommunication against Ulrich for damages and injuries inflicted on the Church of Aquileia and its patriarch by occupying the castle of Wardenech and other castles. Ulrich III (matched) is the principal subject of the excommunication; the counterparties are the ecclesiastical institutions of Aquileia (patriarch and church, unmatched).

persons: Friedrich II von Hohenstaufen, Holy Roman Emperor (subject_or_mention) | Conrad IV von Hohenstaufen, King of Sicily (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the abbots of the monasteries of Mezano and S. Sepulchri in Piacenza to absolve the citizens of Piacenza from excommunication. The citizens had been excommunicated for swearing fealty to Conrad (son of Emperor Frederick II) and accepting Uberto Pallavicino, Frederick's vicar, as their lord. The matched Peerage persons (Frederick II and Conrad IV) appear only as background figures whose past roles triggered the excommunication; the actual parties are the abbots (as papal delegates) and the excommunicated Placentine citizens.

persons: Louis IX, Roi de France (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV responds to the Archbishop of Rouen regarding the jurisdiction of the King of France, barons, and bailiffs of the province of Rouen over lay crusade-signatories (crucesignati). The document addresses the extent of secular authority over crusaders, making crusade protection/jurisdiction the operative matter. Louis IX of France is mentioned as the relevant secular ruler whose jurisdiction is at issue, but he is not a party to a dispute — he appears as a subject of the legal question posed by the Archbishop.

persons: Charles I Stephen d'Anjou, King of Naples and Sicily (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the archdeacon Michael and sacristan Pontius of Maguelone to investigate the value of the jurisdiction of the city of Marseille, what the Count of Provence (Charles of Anjou, matched) has contributed for it, and to what extent the church of Marseille is harmed by the exchange of that jurisdiction. This is an investigative mandate concerning a potential exchange/permutation of ecclesiastical jurisdiction, with the church of Marseille as the principal ecclesiastical party and Charles I of Anjou (Count of Provence) as the lay counterpart. Charles of Anjou appears as the subject of the inquiry (the lay party to the exchange), not as the addressee.

persons: Friedrich II von Hohenstaufen, Holy Roman Emperor (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates officials in the Patrimony of St. Peter, Duchy of Spoleto, Tuscany, Maritima, etc. to compel (via ecclesiastical censures) the podestas, councils, and communes of cities in those regions to inscribe in their statutes the anti-heresy laws promulgated by Emperor Frederick II and sent to them by the Apostolic See. This is a directive concerning heresy legislation enforcement, not a live dispute between parties. Frederick II (matched) is mentioned only as the historical author of the laws in question, not as a party to any conflict.
domain_other_detail: heresy/Inquisition: enforcement of anti-heresy statutes in communal legislation

persons: Louis IX, Roi de France (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to King Louis IX of France (the matched person, as addressee) requesting and urging him to provide counsel and assistance to the brothers of the Order of Humiliati and their envoys, so that the order may be planted and fostered in his kingdom. This is a one-sided papal exhortation/request with no opposing party named; it is a routine act of support for a religious order's expansion.

persons: Ulrich III Herzog von KÃ¤rnten (subject_or_mention) | Philipp Herzog von KÃ¤rnten (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to the abbot and convent of St. Paul in Lavant, declaring that the orders given by Duke Ulrich of Carinthia and his brother Philip (former elect of Salzburg) — forbidding the monastery from receiving letters from Archbishop Ulrich of Salzburg or executing his mandates — are without legal force and not binding on them. The dispute is between the ecclesiastical authority of the Archbishop of Salzburg and the lay interference of Duke Ulrich and Philip of Carinthia. The matched Peerage persons (Duke Ulrich III and Philip of Carinthia) are the lay principals whose prohibition is being invalidated by the pope.

persons: Manfredo I von Hohenstaufen, King of Naples and Sicily (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to the Podestà, council, and commune of Ancona to thank them for their fidelity to the Church. The operative act is a letter of gratitude acknowledging that certain treacherous inhabitants of Faminato (described as weak-spirited and unstable) had conspired to introduce Manfred of Hohenstaufen (matched, as subject of the treachery) into the March of Ancona to the offense of the Apostolic See. The commune of Ancona is the addressee/beneficiary of the papal thanks; Manfred appears only as the named external threat invoked by the traitors, not as a direct party to this document's proceedings.

genre: Titre, général (littere gratiose, cum filo serico)
persons: Gila (?) (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants a marriage dispensation to Maurice, son of William, and Gila, daughter of Maurice de Londres, of the diocese of Ossory, permitting them to remain lawfully in their marriage despite being related in the fourth degree of consanguinity. This is a one-sided grace (dispensation), with no opposing party. Gila is the matched Peerage person, appearing as a co-beneficiary of the dispensation.

persons: Valdemar, King of Sweden (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV urges Valdemar, King of Sweden, and Birger, Count of Sweden, to show reverence to the Archbishop of Uppsala and to restore to his church the villages of Strom, Forne-Situnae, and Quasbro before the archbishop is transferred elsewhere. The dispute is between the Archbishop of Uppsala (unmatched ecclesiastical party) and the Swedish king/count (lay parties) over the restitution of church property. Valdemar, King of Sweden, is a matched principal as addressee and one of the parties ordered to restore the property.

persons: Manfredo I von Hohenstaufen, King of Naples and Sicily (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to the commune of Perugia (podestà, captain, council, and commune) urging them to resist, as they have done before, the forces of Manfred (formerly prince of Taranto), described as a manifest persecutor of the Roman Church, who is attempting to occupy Church lands and has reportedly already invaded the March of Ancona. The pope asks Perugia to provide military support to his relatives Orlando de Ferentino (rector of the Duchy of Spoleto) and Annibaldo (rector of the March of Ancona). Manfred is the matched person but appears only as the named enemy/adversary, not as a party addressed or acting in the document; the principal parties are the papacy/Church and the commune of Perugia on one side against Manfred's forces on the other.

persons: Henry III, King of England (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates his penitentiary and chaplain Walasco (a Franciscan) to induce the King of England, the earls, barons, and other royal councillors to cease molesting Aymer de Valence, the elect of Winchester, and instead allow him to freely collect the revenues and administer his bishopric. The dispute is between the ecclesiastical principal (Aymer, elect of Winchester) and lay parties (the King of England and his nobles). Henry III appears as one of the principal parties being addressed/commanded to desist from the harassment.

persons: Friedrich II von Hohenstaufen, Holy Roman Emperor (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the Prior of S. Maria Magdalena of Val Josaphat to restore the casale of Ferlito in Calabria (with all rights and fruits) to the church of Messina. The operative dispute is between the church of Messina and the legacy of Emperor Frederick II's spoliation: Frederick II had seized the casale from the Messina church after the death of Archbishop Berard of Messina. Friedrich II von Hohenstaufen appears only as the named perpetrator of the original spoliation (subject_or_mention), not as a living party to the current proceeding.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants a privilege to Thibaut, Count of Champagne (matched as Thibaut II/V, King of Navarre): when a general interdict is imposed on his lands, his chaplains may celebrate Mass quietly in his private chapels. This is a one-sided clerical/liturgical privilege granted to a lay noble, with no opposing party. The matched Peerage person (Thibaut) is the sole beneficiary of the grant.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants an indult to Thibaut II, King of Navarre and Count of Champagne, allowing that once the Navarrese have performed the elevation (acclamation) of the king of Navarre, he may assume the royal title and receive unction and coronation at his own pleasure. This is a one-sided papal privilege with no opposing party. Thibaut II is the sole beneficiary and matched principal.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV appoints the abbot of Orbais (diocese of Soissons) and the dean of Tudela (diocese of Tarragona) as conservators of the apostolic privileges granted to Thibaut, count of Champagne (Thibaut II of Navarre). This is a routine administrative mandate establishing protectors of previously granted privileges, with no live dispute. The matched Peerage person, Thibaut II, is the beneficiary of the conservatorship arrangement.

persons: Jaime I, Rey de AragÃ³n (subject_or_mention) | Pedro III, Rey de AragÃ³n (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV confirms a promise made by King James I of Aragon and his son Peter (Count of Barcelona) that they and their heirs will never alter the currency they were then minting. This is a one-sided papal confirmation of a monetary pledge, with no opposing party named. Both matched Peerage persons (James I and Peter/Pedro III) are the beneficiaries/subjects of the confirmation.
domain_other_detail: confirmation of monetary/currency pledge

persons: Alfonso X, Rey de Castilla y LeÃ³n (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants a privilege to Alfonso X, King of Castile and León, stipulating that no papal legate may pronounce a sentence of anathema (excommunication) against him, his wife, his sons, or his ministers without special papal licence. This is a one-sided grant of protection from excommunication, with no opposing party. Alfonso X is the matched beneficiary and sole principal.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants a privilege to Thibaut II, Count of Champagne (and King of Navarre), and his wife: whenever either of them attends a sermon, the preacher may grant one hundred days of indulgence to those present. This is a straightforward one-sided grant of an indulgence privilege with no opposing party. Thibaut II is the matched beneficiary and direct recipient of the grant.

persons: Friedrich II von Hohenstaufen, Holy Roman Emperor (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to the prior and chapter of the cathedral church of St Andrews in Scotland (Augustinian order), requesting that they restore to Peter, clerk and son of George count of Caballiaca, the church of Chinachim, of which his predecessor Innocent IV had deprived him on the grounds that he was said to be a supporter of the late Emperor Frederick II. The document is a papal exhortation/mandate to restore a benefice; the matched person, Emperor Frederick II, appears only as incidental background context (the reason for the original deprivation), not as a party to any live dispute.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants a privilege to Thibaut II, King of Navarre, and the Queen of Navarre (Countess Palatine of Champagne and Brie) and their successors, allowing them to receive unction and coronation from any Catholic bishop in the event that the see of Pamplona is vacant or the Bishop of Pamplona is unwilling or unable to perform the ceremony. This is a one-sided papal indult with no opposing party. Thibaut II is the matched beneficiary and the direct recipient of the privilege.

persons: Valdemar, King of Sweden (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Valdemar, King of Sweden, requesting that he and his subjects provide financial aid and support for the construction of the new Uppsala cathedral church, which is being relocated to a more suitable site. The archbishop and chapter of Uppsala lack sufficient funds for this expensive building project. This is a one-sided papal request/appeal, not a dispute. Valdemar appears as the addressee and target of the papal appeal.

persons: Sophie Eriksdottir, Princess of Denmark (beneficiary) | Christopher I Valdemarsson, King of Denmark (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the archbishops of Uppsala and Linköping and the bishop of Västerås to grant a marriage dispensation to Valdemar, King of Sweden, and Sophie, niece of King Christopher I of Denmark, who are related in the third degree of consanguinity. The document is a routine dispensation for a royal marriage, not a dispute. Sophie is the matched beneficiary; Christopher I is mentioned only as the reference point for Sophie's identity.

persons: Richard, 1st Earl of Cornwall (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to the advocate and council of Aachen (Aquenses) recommending Richard of Cornwall, elected and crowned King of the Romans, urging them to remain faithful to him and offer counsel and aid. The pope extols Richard's virtues, expresses hope that under his leadership the Church and world will enjoy peace, and announces the dispatch of Brother Gualterus de Rogate (Franciscan, papal penitentiary) to convey his intentions more fully. This is a one-sided letter of recommendation/exhortation with no live dispute; Richard of Cornwall (matched) is the subject being commended.

persons: Henry III, King of England (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV informs Henry III, King of England, that he has appointed the Bishop of Elphin as Archbishop of Tuam, and urges the king to assign the regalia of that church to the new archbishop. This is a one-sided papal notification and exhortation, not a live dispute. Henry III appears as the addressee who holds the regalia to be assigned.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants the Dominicans, Franciscans, and other religious attached to the service of Thibaut, Count of Champagne, permission to ride on horseback, wear capes, and use shoes. This is a one-sided privilege/dispensation granted to religious in the count's service, with no dispute involved. Thibaut II (V) of Navarre appears as the subject/context (the lord whose household clergy receive the privilege), not as a party to any conflict.

persons: Henry III, King of England (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Henry III, King of England, requesting and urging him to grant the Bishop of Rochester (who is occupied at the Apostolic See on business of the king and the Roman Empire and cannot personally travel to England) a procurator (an "attorney" in the royal court) to represent him in his absence. The operative matter is an ongoing legal dispute between the Bishop of Rochester and the Archbishop of Canterbury over certain articles being litigated in the royal court. Henry III is the addressee/principal being petitioned; the real disputants are the Bishop of Rochester and the Archbishop of Canterbury, neither of whom is a matched Peerage person.

persons: Agnes 'the Saint' of Bohemia (requestor)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants a privilege to the Franciscan friars of Wrocław and Agnes of Bohemia (sister of the monastery of St. Francis in Prague) and the abbess of the convent of St. Clare in Wrocław, allowing the friars to come to the convent window to converse with the abbess on matters useful to the nuns. This is a one-sided grant/concession with no opposing party. Agnes of Bohemia appears as a co-petitioner/requestor alongside the Franciscan friars and the abbess of St. Clare's.

persons: Richard, 1st Earl of Cornwall (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Richard, Earl of Cornwall and King of the Romans elect, praising his longstanding defense of ecclesiastical liberty and noting that his coronation and unction have already taken place. The pope announces he is sending Brother Walter de Rogat, his familiar and penitentiary, specially to Germany to govern in Richard's favor and to instruct all princes of the empire — both those adhering to Richard and those not — to remain or come into his fidelity. The pope asks Richard to receive Walter benignly and to excuse his other nuncios for their long stay at the curia. This is a one-sided papal communication/mandate in support of Richard's imperial position, with no live dispute as the operative matter.
domain_other_detail: papal political support / diplomatic mandate to imperial princes

persons: Richard, 1st Earl of Cornwall (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Conrad, Archbishop of Cologne, urging him to remain faithful and devoted to Richard, King of the Romans, whom Conrad himself had elected and anointed. This is a one-sided papal exhortation/mandate addressed to the archbishop, with no live dispute between opposing parties. Richard of Cornwall (1st Earl of Cornwall, King of the Romans) is mentioned as the subject of the loyalty being urged, not as a party to a conflict.

persons: Friedrich II von Hohenstaufen, Holy Roman Emperor (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the bishops of Pavia and Maino and the prior of the Dominican friars of Pavia to absolve the podestà, council, and people of the city of Pavia from ecclesiastical censures, on condition that they swear to abide by the Church's commands, as they are returning to the Church after having followed the late Emperor Frederick II. The operative act is the lifting of excommunication/censures from the Pavians. Frederick II (matched) appears only as a historical reference — the cause of the original censures — not as a party to the present proceeding.

persons: Premysl II Ottokar, King of Bohemia (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV confirms by apostolic authority the liberties, exemptions from secular exactions, revenues, and other rights granted by King Ottokar II of Bohemia (6 June 1252) to the master and brethren of St. Francis in Prague (Augustinian order) for both their hospital and the church of St. Hippolytus in Gradicz near Znojmo. This is a straightforward papal confirmation of a prior royal grant, with no dispute involved. King Ottokar II (Premysl II) appears only as the original donor whose grant is being confirmed, not as a party to any conflict.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (requestor)
summary: Pope Alexander IV grants, at the request of King Thibaut II of Navarre, that all students studying at the schools in Thibaut's castle of Tudela (diocese of Tarazona) may receive their ecclesiastical revenues with the same fullness as those studying in Paris. This is a one-sided privilege/indulgence with no opposing party. Thibaut II appears as the requestor/beneficiary of the grant.

persons: BÃ©la IV ArpÃ¡d, King of Hungary (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Archbishop Benedict of Esztergom (Strigoniensis), instructing him to deliver apostolic letters to King Béla IV of Hungary citing him to Rome, and to urge the king to fulfil his late father's promise to pay 1,000 marks of silver annually to the master and brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem (Knights Hospitaller), and to observe their privileges, immunities, and agreements. The dispute is between the Hospitaller Order (an ecclesiastical institution) and King Béla IV (a lay ruler) over the unpaid annual payment and violated privileges. Béla IV appears as the subject of the mandate — the party being cited and pressured — while the Hospitallers are the unmatched ecclesiastical counterparty.

persons: Christopher I Valdemarsson, King of Denmark (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the bishops of Schwerin, Lübeck, and Paderborn to admonish and induce Christopher I, King of Denmark, to restore Archbishop Jacob of Lund, the provost, and the archdeacon of Lund to their former liberty within one month and allow them to depart freely. The dispute is between the King of Denmark (lay) and the Archbishop and chapter of Lund (ecclesiastical). The matched Peerage person, Christopher I, is the principal lay party being ordered to release the ecclesiastical captives.

persons: Henry III, King of England (addressee) | Alexander III 'the Glorius', King of Scotland (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to Henry III, King of England, asking him to persuade Alexander III, King of Scotland, to grant the regalia/temporalities to John of Cheam, the newly elected Bishop of Glasgow (formerly the pope's chaplain and Archdeacon of Bath), without delay. This is a one-sided papal request/mandate, not a live dispute; the operative act is facilitating the conferral of temporal endowment on a newly appointed bishop.

persons: Johann I Graf von Holstein (subject_or_mention) | Gerhard I Graf von Holstein-Itzehoe (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the abbot and prior of St. Michael's monastery (Benedictine, Hildesheim) to compel Johann I and Gerhard I, counts of Holstein, to restore the town of Hamburg to the chapter and church of Bremen. The town had been unjustly granted to the counts by Archbishop Gerhard of Bremen. The dispute is between the Bremen cathedral chapter/church (ecclesiastical) and the two Holstein counts (lay). The matched Peerage persons — Johann I and Gerhard I of Holstein — are the principal lay parties being compelled to make restitution.

persons: Johann I Graf von Holstein (subject_or_mention) | Gerhard I Graf von Holstein-Itzehoe (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates the abbot and prior of St. Michael's monastery (Benedictine, Hildesheim) to compel the consuls and commune of Hamburg, through sentences of excommunication and interdict, to return to the devotion and fidelity of the church of Bremen and to answer to the Archbishop of Bremen for his rights and revenues. The dispute is between the Archbishop of Bremen (ecclesiastical principal) and the commune of Hamburg (lay principal), with the counts of Holstein (Johann I and Gerhard I) mentioned only as the lords whose dominion Hamburg is to abandon — they appear as incidental background parties, not as principal disputants.

persons: Thibaut II (V), Rey de Navarre (beneficiary)
summary: Pope Alexander IV appoints the abbot of Orbais (diocese of Soissons) and the dean of Tudela (diocese of Tarragona) as conservators of the apostolic privileges granted to Thibaut, count of Champagne (Thibaut II of Navarre). This is a one-sided administrative mandate appointing guardians of privileges; no dispute is involved. Thibaut II appears as the beneficiary whose privileges are being protected.

persons: BÃ©la IV ArpÃ¡d, King of Hungary (subject_or_mention)
summary: Pope Alexander IV mandates Benedict, Archbishop of Esztergom (Strigonium), under pain of excommunication, to admonish and persuade King Béla IV of Hungary to pay 1,000 marks to the Knights Hospitaller (fratres hospitalis Ierosolymitani), as stipulated in earlier papal letters of 10 June 1258. The archbishop is to report back within six months. The operative dispute/obligation is between the King of Hungary and the Hospitallers over the payment of these marks; Béla IV appears as the subject of the mandate (the party to be pressured), not as a matched principal in the dispute itself.

persons: Louis IX, Roi de France (addressee)
summary: Pope Alexander IV writes to King Louis IX of France (the matched person, as addressee) requesting and urging him to lend the force of royal power to Reginald, Bishop of Paris, whenever called upon, in order to suppress and punish those who disturb the University of Paris.
